findings.description: Blog post title retains old HRCB context word 'Compatibility' after the expansion standardization commit. Title reads 'Validating HRCB: Can LLMs Measure Human Rights Compatibility?' while the body (lines 32, 51) now defines HRCB as 'Human Rights Covenant Baseline.' The commit (08025c34) standardized the expansion in the body and vocabulary section but missed the title. Readers encountering 'Compatibility' in the title and 'Covenant Baseline' in the body experience a within-document vocabulary inconsistency.
findings.suggestion: Update the title to 'Validating HRCB: Can LLMs Measure Human Rights Alignment?' or 'Validating HRCB: Can LLMs Score Human Rights Content?' — avoiding both the old expansion and the new one (since 'Covenant Baseline' does not read naturally as a title question). Alternatively, use 'Validating the Human Rights Covenant Baseline' if the acronym expansion should appear in the title.
findings.context: title: "Validating HRCB: Can LLMs Measure Human Rights Compatibility?"

findings.description: E-prime violation in the voter-only evidence card description. This line existed before the current commit range — pre-existing issue surfaced during full-file scan.
findings.suggestion: Rephrase to eliminate 'is': 'Enforceable rights prevent exactly this — communities absorbing these costs without protection.' Or: 'Communities absorbing these costs without protection demonstrates the gap enforceable rights close.'
findings.context: Communities absorbing these costs without protection is precisely what enforceable rights prevent — the data on AI spending, job losses, and healthcare cuts.
